links.outcome: Model discrimination and net benefit when extended to consecutive daily prediction beyond 48 h
links.effect: fullPIERS AUC-PRC stayed low (0.2-0.4); PIERS-ML AUC-PRC peaked at 0.65 on day 0 then decreased notably; decision curve advantage diminished over time.
links.quote: We observed deteriorating performance of both models over time.

links.outcome: Performance of models used outside intended initial-assessment use (repeated use past 48 h)
links.effect: PIERS-ML performance declined notably for most risk groups beyond 48 h; fullPIERS AUC-PRC (0.2-0.4) close to daily fraction of adverse outcomes, indicating low discriminative capacity.
links.quote: We recommend using the models for consecutive prediction with greater caution and interpreting predictions with increasing uncertainty as the pregnancy progresses.

screen.reason: Evaluates the recommended clinical practice of using static risk models consecutively/serially over time post-admission, demonstrating model drift and performance decay.
